title.value: On the relation between the sharpest directions of DNN loss and the SGD step length
title.justification: The title is clearly stated at the beginning of the paper and reflects the main focus of the research, which is to investigate the relationship between sharp directions of deep neural network loss and the stochastic gradient descent step length.
title.quote: On the relation between the sharpest directions of DNN loss and the SGD step length

analysis.description: This paper investigates the dynamics of stochastic gradient descent (SGD) in relation to the sharpest directions of the loss surface in deep neural networks (DNNs). Specifically, it examines how these sharp directions influence regions visited by SGD, training speed, and generalization ability. The study finds that a reduced learning rate along sharp directions can optimize faster and lead to better solutions. The research exposes that SGD initially visits sharp regions, influenced by learning rate and batch size, and proposes an SGD variant with a reduced learning rate along sharp directions to improve optimization.

type.justification: The paper presents empirical investigations and experiments on models like Resnet-32, SimpleCNN, VGG-11, and LSTM with datasets such as CIFAR-10 and PTB to study the dynamics of SGD related to Hessian eigenvalues.
type.quote: An empirical investigation shows that initially SGD visits increasingly sharp regions, reaching a maximum sharpness determined by both the learning rate and the batch-size of SGD.
